title: The Sunstone's Secret Journey
markdown:
The scent of dried lavender and damp earth always clung to Pippa’s small cottage, familiar, comforting. Today the air buzzed with a different kind of magic. A soft glow, like sunlight caught on morning dew, bloomed around a small stone that had landed with a gentle thud in her prize moonpetals. No ordinary stone. Warm. Surface swirling with colours like the sky at dawn. The Sunstone: the heart that kept the mountain passes clear and the streams bright. Its light, meant for the High Shrine, had found her quiet garden.

Bunting, Pippa’s marmot friend, popped from his burrow, chattering.

“Oh dear me, oh my. That’s the Sunstone. It should be on the High Shrine, not here. And the mountain passes, Pippa, they’re already fading into that awful mist.”

Unease. The stories said the Sunstone returned to the High Shrine at the Solstice to keep the passes clear. Now, by accident, it was her responsibility. A heavy feeling in her stomach, a flutter strange for someone who handled stubborn mandrakes with steady hands. The High Shrine was usually a two-day journey. Dawn was coming. If the Sunstone was not returned, the mountains would be lost in a chilling mist, cutting off the valley villages.

“Well, Bunting,” Pippa said, dusting dirt from her hands, calm, practical, “it seems we have a journey to take. And it needs to be a quick one.” She placed the Sunstone in a soft pouch. Warmth a constant reminder.

A large gentle shadow. Ignis, a young dragon with scales like polished emeralds, landed with barely a whisper. Manners always perfect.

“Good day, Mistress Pippa, Master Bunting.” Distant thunder softened by velvet. “Might I ask about the urgency of your current ground-level location? And the unusual glow coming from your person?”

Pippa explained, holding up the Sunstone. Ignis bowed his magnificent head.

“A matter of great importance. The Whispering Peaks are indeed being covered by mist. I would be honoured to help you on your urgent trip to the High Shrine.”

Their journey began quickly. Pine shadows stretched long and dark. The sun sank, fiery oranges and deep purples. Crisp air, pine needles. Winding trails, steeper. Bunting clung to Pippa’s shoulder, small paws batting, peering at the drop.

Around a sharp turn, a huge figure blocked the path. Siobhan Buttercup, an ogre shepherd, thick arms crossed, weathered face surprisingly smart. Pippa prepared for grump. Ogres were not known for talking or helping.

“Evening, Pippa,” Siobhan rumble, pebbles shifting. “Off to the High Shrine, are you? And in a hurry, I see. The mist is already creeping down the lower slopes.”

Pippa blinked. He knew her name and destination. “How did you know?”

Siobhan pointed a thumb at the Sunstone, which she had taken from its pouch. “That light. It’s not natural, not for this time of day. And you, marmot, look more jumpy than a rabbit in a fox den.” He squinted. “There’s something strange about that one, too. It looks like it has a seam, almost invisible. Almost like it was made in two parts.”

Pippa, always one to observe, brought the stone closer. He was right. A faint line, almost hidden by swirling colours, ran around it. She had been so focused on meaning, warmth, power, that she had missed a simple detail. A gentle push of her finger. A slight give. A tiny compartment, no bigger than a ladybug, clicked open. Inside: a single delicate silver feather, shimmering with its own soft light.

She had been so focused on the Sunstone’s big meaning and the rush to return it that she had missed its hidden secrets. A strong urge to ignore Siobhan’s sharp eyes, to pretend it was a lucky guess. The feather, unexpected, changed the day.

“A silver feather,” she murmured. “What could this mean? Part of the ritual? A key, maybe?”

Ignis, polite, thoughtful: “Perhaps, Mistress Pippa, it is a key, or part of an old spell to make the Sunstone’s power stronger.” Dry humour, sincere. A faint smile.

The real challenge was not an ogre or a dark wizard or a mysterious feather. As they neared the ancient wind-worn stones of the High Shrine, a low groaning echoed through the canyon. A part of the old structure, weakened by wind and frost, began to crumble. Rocks, some as large as sheep, rained down with a terrifying clatter, threatening to block the path and, worse, shatter the shrine itself.

No time for grand speeches or complicated spells. Pippa’s magic came from the earth and the quiet needs of growing things. She saw the crumbling wall, the falling stones, the impossibility of reaching the shrine’s top. She saw her small leather pouch of moonpetal seeds, carefully grown for a year, each seed holding stored moonlight: a year of gentle tending, watering under pale moonlight, whispering encouragement. The shrine, the heart of the mountains, was in greater danger. The mist was now a cold thick presence around their ankles.

A quick movement. She unfastened the pouch. Cool mountain air. Rough gritty crumbling stone under her fingertips. Faint sweet almost-magical scent of moonpetals. She scattered the seeds. Pale glow against dust and gloom. They caught on the edges of the stones, magic weaving a temporary shimmering hold, fairy threads keeping rocks together.

“Hold,” she whispered, as if to a wilting flower.

The stones paused. The groaning stopped. The rockslide halted, held by the new magic of the moonpetals. A personal cost. Needed.

As dawn painted rose and gold, Pippa, Bunting safely on a ledge, placed the Sunstone on its ancient pedestal. A wave of pure warm light. The mist that had crept down the passes vanished with surprising speed. Streams below sparkled, cheerful gurgle a song of relief.

Pippa, Bunting, and Ignis watched, quiet satisfaction like a warm cloak. Siobhan Buttercup, sitting on a nearby ridge where he had been watching everything, gave a slow almost invisible nod, eyes crinkling. He understood. Unity restored not by battle but by looking closely, and by giving up a year’s seeds. Bunting, surprisingly, had not fainted even once. Ignis, with a final graceful bow that sent a ripple of emerald across his scales, remarked, “A most interesting trip, Mistress Pippa. One hopes the moonpetals will forgive their early departure and can perhaps be replanted a little sooner next season.”

Pippa smiled, fond thought for wilting seedlings mixed with a job done. Lavender and damp earth already beginning to return as they turned toward home, tired, the pouch empty, the passes clear.
characters: Pippa (witch), Bunting (marmot), Ignis (young dragon), Siobhan Buttercup (ogre shepherd)
audience: teenagers aged 13-15, amusing distant-lands fantasy for independent readers
